Why make a separate copy of the protocol names? Doesn't disabled_proto_names always have to be in sync with global_disabled_protos and disabled_protos?

Yes but in proto.c we need to do a lookup in the list to see if the the protocol is in the list of dissabled protocols. This lookup

needs to be fast hence a hashtable.
No, I agree with adding the hashtable, I just don't think the protocol_def structure needs to be duplicated.

This can be called in ProtocolHierarchyDialog::on_actionRevertProtos_triggered, but the corresponding cleanup_enabled_and_disabled_lists is never called in the dialog - only epan_cleanup(), so that looks like it could be a "leak" or out of sync lists.
I get that we have potentially separate source file(s) of disabled protocols, but why do we need two lists?  They don't do anything different and are always passed together.
Not sure - not my code - global and personal profiles?

Yes, but your new code doesn't handle the case where only one of the two changes (because the hash table will get out of sync).  My suggestion would be to have this MR consolidate to a single list (for iteration) and hash table (for quick lookup) all while reading the two files that have disabled protocol lists.
The lists are never written, only read so that's why they don't need to be separate.
I believe this comment goes with the function above (there is no reading done in this function)
What does reading the disabled protocol file(s) early get us?  Aren't protocols in the proper enabled/disabled state by the time a capture file is loaded?
The whole purpose of this change is to be able to skip stuff when registering protocols, see proto_register_field_array().

But is the code run to later register the fields if you enable the protocol again?  There seem to be different "levels" of enable/disable and that could be confusing to the user (it's certainly confusing me).  Does this "disabling" (via file) mean you permanently never want the dissector loaded, whereas the Enabled Protocols dialog is only temporary to that session of Wireshark?
For this to work properly one would need to re-run epan_init I suppose. Not sur why we have a enabled and a dissabled protocol list.
